citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
Indicatif renders through write_str on this unit-test-only adapter.
 TermLike also requires write_line, whose only behavior delegates to
 that covered recording path. No application input can select this
 unused adapter callback; actual terminal output is tested on a PTY.

rationale:
The `habeas:coverage` citation on `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/impl[RecordingTerm/indicatif::TermLike]/fn[write_line]` is acceptable.

- **Placement and form:** The citation is on an explicit function with a body. The explanation sits in fenced `:::{cite}` commentary, which the built-in text accepts. The built-in permits `cite` here, and no `impl` or `test` reference conflicts with it.
- **Substantive reason:** The commentary gives a real justification, not just difficulty. The adapter is a unit-test-only `TermLike` implementation. The trait requires `write_line`, and the test path does not use it. The commentary also says terminal output is verified on a PTY.
- **Agreement with source:** `write_line` only calls `self.write_str(&format!("{text}\n"))`. That matches the "only behavior delegates" claim. `write_str` in the same impl records the text and frames, and the tests `stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared` and `preparation_activity_keeps_updating_without_a_stage_change` exercise it, so it counts as the covered recording path. `RecordingTerm` is declared inside `mod[tests]`, so no application input can reach it. No `.write_line(` call exists under `src`.
- **Limit of my check:** I could not read the indicatif source, so "Indicatif renders through write_str" rests on the commentary and on what I recall of indicatif's drawing code. The exception can remain even if coverage turns out to be measured, so this does not affect the outcome.

I found no gap.
